references.text: Moses sent out men to spy out the land of Canaan, which is the background for the events in chapter 14.
The spies returned and spread a malicious report (דִבָּה) about the land, which led to the people's rebellion.
The congregation grumbled and complained against Moses and Aaron after hearing the spies' report.
The immediate consequence for the men who spread the evil report about the land was that they died by a plague.
Moses recounts the event of sending out the spies and their negative report about the land.
The psalmist refers to how the people despised the pleasant land and grumbled in their tents, not believing in the Lord's word.
Hebrews refers to the wilderness generation that sinned and was not allowed to enter into rest because of unbelief.
Paul warns against grumbling as some of the Israelites did and were killed by the destroyer.
